Query: Is Button worth it for ecommerce businesses?
Response:
Button can be worth it for ecommerce businesses, but mainly for brands that already have meaningful mobile, app, affiliate, creator, or publisher-driven traffic. It is not a general ecommerce store builder or basic marketing tool.

Verdict

Worth considering if:

You sell at scale and care about mobile conversion, especially app-to-web or web-to-app journeys.

You already run, or plan to run, affiliate / creator / publisher commerce programs.

You have enough volume that improving post-click conversion and attribution can move revenue materially.

You want hands-on support for commerce media, deep linking, app installs, or affiliate optimization.

Button describes itself as a platform for brands to improve mobile marketing and ad performance using identity, deep linking, and machine learning. Its Full Service Network is positioned as a way for retailers and publishers to launch and optimize affiliate programs, with AI-powered routing toward higher-converting purchase journeys. 
Button
 
Button

Probably not worth it if:

You are a small ecommerce business still trying to get consistent traffic.

You do not have a mobile app or meaningful mobile commerce volume.

You mainly need email/SMS, Shopify apps, checkout optimization, or basic affiliate tracking.

You need transparent self-serve pricing before evaluating vendors; Button’s public pages emphasize demo/contact flows rather than publishing simple fixed plans. 
Button

Why it could be valuable

Button’s core value is reducing friction after a shopper clicks: better deep links, app routing, tracking, and conversion optimization. That matters because affiliate and creator traffic often underperforms when users land in the wrong place, lose attribution, or get pushed into lower-converting flows. Button claims large-scale commerce results, including surpassing $25B in all-time gross merchandise sales on the platform and 91% year-over-year growth in app-driven sales in 2025. 
Button

It also appears especially relevant to larger ecommerce companies with mobile apps and affiliate/creator programs. A PRNewswire release states Button’s customers include creators, publishers, and “large ecommerce companies with mobile apps” focused on affiliate and creator marketing. 
PR Newswire

Practical recommendation

For a mid-market or enterprise ecommerce brand, Button is worth evaluating if you can answer “yes” to at least two of these:

Question	Why it matters
Do we have a mobile app?	Button’s strongest claims center on app-driven commerce and deep linking.
Do we already spend on affiliate, creator, or publisher traffic?	Button optimizes that traffic rather than replacing demand generation.
Are we losing conversion between click and checkout?	Post-tap routing is where Button seems differentiated.
Is attribution quality a pain point?	Broken or messy tracking is a common reason to use a platform like this.
Is incremental revenue large enough to justify enterprise-style pricing?	Public materials suggest a demo-led sales motion, so ROI likely depends on scale.

For a small ecommerce business, I would usually prioritize lower-friction tools first: Shopify-native affiliate apps, Klaviyo/Omnisend for lifecycle marketing, Google/Meta/TikTok shopping integrations, and landing-page or checkout optimization. Button becomes more compelling once affiliate/creator traffic is already large enough that even a small lift in conversion or attribution creates meaningful revenue.

Bottom line

Button is worth it for ecommerce businesses with scale, mobile traffic, and affiliate/creator programs. It is likely overkill for early-stage stores that still need basic acquisition, retention, and conversion tools.

Query: How does Button handle deep linking?
Response:
Button handles deep linking by routing a mobile click to the destination most likely to convert, rather than treating every link as a static URL.

How it works:

Smart routing at click time
Button evaluates the tap and routes the user to the best destination. Button says its platform identifies and routes users to the “highest-converting destination,” with an emphasis on sending users into apps when that is expected to perform better. 
Button

App-first behavior when the app is installed
For PostTap links, Button says the link can open the correct page inside the app when the app is already installed. For example, with Amazon traffic, PostTap connects the click to the installed Amazon app and determines the best destination for the consumer. 
PostTap

Web fallback when the app is not installed
If the relevant app is not installed, Button says the click redirects to the destination on the web instead of failing. 
PostTap

Deferred deep linking for app installs
Button’s Android SDK documentation includes deferred deep-link handling. The app calls checkForDeepLink on first launch after installation; if Button finds a pending deferred deep link, it invokes onDeepLink(Intent) with a VIEW intent. The app can then start that intent and read the pending deep link data in the target Activity. 
Building Button

No-code options for creators/publishers
PostTap is described as cloud-based and does not require technical development to start; creators can create shortlinks that apply Button’s deep-linking and routing logic. 
PostTap

Bottom line: Button’s deep linking is designed to turn affiliate or commerce links into optimized mobile journeys: open the product/page in-app when possible, fall back to web when needed, and support deferred deep linking after app install for SDK-based integrations.
